claim: Pirolli and Card 2005 present a notional two-loop model (foraging loop, sensemaking loop, six data stores, back loops at every level) derived from a preliminary cognitive task analysis of several intelligence analysts, with no reported sample size, counts or effect sizes; no direct test or replication of the whole model was found in this search.
agent_test: Tag each agent step as forage or sense and check that logging the loop name alone changes nothing; then test forced alternation vs free mixing at equal tokens.
audit_note: The paper itself confirms a notional, preliminary model (two loops, six data stores, back loops, no sample size or statistics, derived from interviews and protocols with several analysts); but a01-a03 are one document, and 'never been tested as a whole' rests only on a failed search note (a31), not on a source.
claim_before_audit: Pirolli and Card 2005 is a notional two-loop model (foraging loop, sensemaking loop, six data stores, back loops at every level) with no reported sample, counts or effect sizes; it has never been tested as a whole.

claim: Explore/enrich/exploit narrowing of the foraging loop (precision-recall trade-off) is a design claim only; no measured test in humans.
agent_test: Compare a wide-then-narrow retrieval budget vs flat budget at equal tokens on multi-hop QA.

claim: Explicit, separate epistemic state plus hierarchical forage actions helps long-document answering: SCOUT about 78 (78.7 main table, 78.2 ablation table) at 29.7k tokens vs Gemini-3-Pro 68.5 at 273.9k; removing the epistemic state costs 7.7 points, removing document access 60.5.
agent_test: Ablate a written evidence-state note in our agent on long-context tasks at fixed token cap.
note: Equal-cost evidence: w/o epistemic state 70.5 at 28.3k vs full 78.2 at 29.7k. Long-document tasks only; in-context tasks untested.

claim: Information-scent rewards in RL for search agents improve results: InForage 41.0 mean EM vs Search-o1 35.6, plain RAG 26.5 on a 3B model.
agent_test: Add a gain-per-retrieval check (did the last fetch add a new fact?) and stop on low gain; measure accuracy per token.
note: Prompt-only scent/yield patch switching (PatchScout) also beats no-switch and a trained agent at matched tokens on broad topics, but a fixed-count switch is nearly as good and the trained agent wins on one sparse topic. Different task (corpus collection).

claim: LLM overviews of a topic speed up and widen human sensemaking in small within-subject studies (Selenite 36.3% faster, recall 73.0 vs 30.4; Sensecape 68.3 vs 22.8 concepts explored) but N is 12 and these are not agent accuracy tests.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as motive for structured overview step before deep dive.
audit_note: Minor: the Sensecape metric is concepts explored (not speed), with a very large SD (49.1); Selenite recall 73.0 vs 30.4% refers to externalised criteria; Selenite also had a separate N=8 open study.

claim: Faster is not more accurate: Marco was 16% faster (249.6 vs 297.3 s) but slightly less accurate (88.1 vs 91.9%, p=.067); Sensecape users preferred baseline for broad understanding (6 of 12).
agent_test: Report speed and accuracy separately; require accuracy parity before accepting a shortcut.
audit_note: Minor: the accuracy difference (88.1 vs 91.9%, p=.067) is not significant, so only slightly less accurate, not significantly is supported.

claim: Structured analytic technique ACH did not improve analyst accuracy in the one controlled test with analysts: MAE 0.26 vs control 0.21, d=0.43, p=.14, N=50.
agent_test: Run ACH-style matrix vs free reasoning at equal tokens on diagnosis items; expect null.
note: For LLMs: ACH-matrix prompt gives a small gain (+2.0 vs single agent on knowledge MCQs) and explicit hypothesis plus counterfactual critique gives +6 to +7 on diagnosis (CIs overlap, not token matched). Human null stays.

claim: ACH users judged evidence usefulness more accurately in rating (d=1.59) but this did not track accuracy of their final forecasts (r=-.10), and ACH did not reduce unpacking bias.
agent_test: Check whether a matrix step improves final answer, not only the stated rationale.

claim: Post-hoc coherence correction of probability judgments cuts error by 35% (0.23 to 0.15), 61% with aggregation.
agent_test: Force sum-to-one on hypothesis probabilities after the agent answers; compare Brier at equal tokens.

claim: ACH training in 191 law students did not change preference: both groups preferred exonerating questions; Lehner 2008 found no ACH effect on analysts.
agent_test: See K07.
audit_note: Minor: Lehner 2008 is known only through Mandel et al.s secondhand summary (ACH reduced confirmation bias in non-analysts but had no effect on analysts); Maegherman also concluded participants failed to apply ACH properly.

claim: LLMs confirm rather than falsify: rule-discovery success ranges 6% to 78% across 11 models, and prompts that raise the incompatible-test ratio help thinking models (Qwen3-8B 0.21 to 0.36 with Think-in-Opposites, 0.40 with Dual-Goal; Qwen3-32B 0.41 to 0.61, p<2e-5) but not reliably non-thinking ones (Dual-Goal -0.06, p=.0065). A second task (Blicket) gives mixed direction.
agent_test: Add a 'propose a test that would break the leading hypothesis' step; measure incompatible-test ratio and success at equal turns.
note: Qwen3-32B figure fixed to 0.41 to 0.61 (gap 5 closed). Same authors for both tasks; no independent replication; token totals per solved episode not reported.

claim: Single-pass LLM sensemaking loses detail and facts: holistic GPT-4 covered 6 of the key facts with 0 comprehensive vs crowd 17; step-by-step 9 (5 comprehensive); hypotheses 10 vs 4 but crowd's fully comprehensive.
agent_test: Compare holistic vs step-by-step fact extraction at equal tokens on a fixed case with an answer key.

claim: Corpus-level sensemaking by graph summaries beats vector RAG on global questions (comprehensiveness win rate 72-83%, p<.001).
agent_test: Test a community-summary memory vs flat retrieval on global questions.

claim: Context quantity matters for grounded synthesis: hallucination-free rate rises from about 40% (15k chars) to about 85% (30k) in a financial-news workflow; blind test 3 of 12 accepted vs 0 of 10.
agent_test: Vary retrieved-context size at fixed output; note blind-test N is tiny.

claim: Constraining sensemaking order (hindsight) gives +2.0% plan quality and more diversity than foresight across 8 model families.
agent_test: Test hindsight-style synthesis vs foresight at equal tokens; effect is small.

claim: ACT-R model of the data-frame sensemaking tasks matches humans on most of 6 tasks (S1 within about 10 points in 5 of 6 cells) but misses resource allocation in Task 3 (34.7 vs 73.8).
agent_test: Not an LLM test; background.

claim: Large display space changed how people structured their workspace (n=16, 8 per group): more structures, 15.75 vs 9 (p=.004, t-tests with alpha .1), with coverage only borderline (18.53% vs 13.12%, p=.061) and no significant difference in analytic score.
agent_test: Give agent a persistent structured workspace vs flat scratchpad.
audit_note: Table 4.1 comes from a 16-subject study (8 per condition), not N=8 total, and the same study found no difference in analytic score, so 'helps human sensemaking' is wider than the data (more structures only; alpha was set at p<0.1).
claim_before_audit: Large display space helps human sensemaking: structures 15.75 vs 9 (p=.004) with N=8; borderline for coverage.

claim: Human-AI team gains over best individual are not guaranteed, and many 2024-2026 papers on analyst sensemaking with LLMs are position papers without measurements.
agent_test: Treat as a weak-evidence warning.
audit_note: Minor: 'many' rests on three papers (Cheng and Houben workshop position paper, Patterson AFRL conceptual paper, Jain research agenda); Jain says teams 'do not yet reliably outperform the best individual'.

claim: SOC field data: 45 analysts issued 3,090 LLM queries in 10 months, 93% map to NICE competencies, mostly 1-3 turns.
agent_test: Descriptive only.

claim: Human-like semantic foraging patch-switching is linearly decodable from LLM activations (AUC 0.72 anticipatory, 0.87 event).
agent_test: Interpretability evidence, not a scaffold test.
audit_note: Both papers share co-author Peter M. Todd and are sibling studies of the same task (semantic fluency); the AUC values 0.72/0.87 come from the first paper alone and are maximum values for Gemma-9B only; the second paper's probe on real human sequences was weak (AUROC 0.57) and only strong on contrastive datasets (0.96-0.98).

claim: SHELDON, a general dual-search (hypothesis and observation) harness, scores 84.00 on DiagnosisArena vs 78.00 for RLM and 76.00 for Codex; separately, EviDx's evidence scaffold with an observer harness improves multiple-choice diagnosis over its single-agent baseline (e.g. Qwen3-8B 18% to 44% on JAMA) while open-ended diagnosis stays limited.
agent_test: Note different backbones and 100-case subsets; replicate with our model.
audit_note: Numbers are right (SHELDON 84.00 vs RLM 78.00, Codex 76.00), but SHELDON is a general scientific-reasoning harness (diagnosis, root-cause, ARC-AGI-2), EviDx has no dual search, and EviDx's baseline is its own single agent with gains clearest on multiple choice and open-ended diagnosis still limited.
claim_before_audit: Medical diagnosis agents with scaffolded evidence gathering and dual search over hypotheses and observations beat baselines (SHELDON DiagnosisArena 84.00 vs 78.00).

claim: Qwen3-32B figures in Failing to Falsify are 0.413 (baseline) to 0.613 (Think-in-Opposites) and 0.600 (Dual-Goal) for the thinking model; the 0.33 to 0.63 reading was wrong.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: An explicit hypothesis-and-evidence record with a counterfactual critic improves LLM diagnosis over the same backbone without it: SIA 79.2 vs 72.8 (interactive thinking) and 67.5 (thinking only); removing the critic costs 5.2 points, removing the structured state 6.4; numeric weight updates cost only 0.7.
agent_test: Ablate the critic and the written state at equal tokens on our diagnosis items; skip numeric weights.

claim: A zero-shot ACH-style hypothesis-evidence matrix prompt for the deciding agent adds about 2 points over a single agent and 1.9 over an unstructured decider on knowledge MCQs; a rigid scaffold learned alone is worse than a plain prompt (Scaffolding-Only 68.1 vs vanilla 72.6 on MMLU).
agent_test: Allow deviation from the matrix; test on items with several plausible answers.

claim: Prompt-only information-scent patch switching raises coverage over no switching (Universities 1.7 to 15.5, Law 1.0 to 86.8) and beats a trained search agent at matched tokens on 3 of 4 topics, but a fixed-count switch gets most of the gain and the trained agent wins on the sparse Autism topic (17.3 vs 12.8).
agent_test: Compare fixed-budget switch vs gain-per-fetch switch at equal tokens.

claim: DeepNews context-size cliff (40% at 15k characters, 85% at 30k) is one-factor and not decomposed into redundancy vs volume; 20 reports per cell with no variance.
agent_test: Run a volume-held, redundancy-varied test before adopting any size rule.

claim: Pirolli and Card Figure 6 (experts gain information faster) is a notional graph with no data; the claim has no measured support in the sources opened.
agent_test: No scaffold element.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors
